Answer: D
Reason: Visual inspection of the chest X-ray reveals bilateral, patchy airspace opacities predominantly located in the peripheral and lower lung zones, which is the classic radiographic pattern for cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP). Although the automated report describes a "stable right upper lobe nodular opacity" and denies focal consolidation, this contradicts the obvious bilateral peripheral findings visible on the image; per skill t000002, the visual morphology of peripheral/basal consolidation takes precedence over the hallucinated or limited text report when identifying COP.
